items.title: Disclosure of Pecuniary Interest and the General Nature Thereof
notes: No disclosure of pecuniary interest was declared by any member of Council at this point in the meeting.

items.title: Territorial Acknowledgement
notes: Councillor Wright opened the meeting with the following Territorial Acknowledgement:

We would like to begin by acknowledging that the land on which we gather (land on which we are broadcasting from) today is the land traditionally cared for by the Haudenosaunee, Anishinaabe and Chonnontan People. We also acknowledge the enduring presence and deep traditional knowledge and philosophies of the Indigenous People with whom we share this land today.

items.title: Moment of Reflection
notes: Councillor Wright provided Council with a moment of reflection.
At the beginning of this Council meeting, we pause to think about the needs of our community. May we show wisdom and compassion in all our decisions.

Michael Pugliese responded to questions of Council.

items.title: Zoning By-law Amendment Z-26-11
notes: Amanda Wyszynski gave a presentation outlining the proposed development, including the conceptual renderings and the planning framework. She then responded to questions of Council.
Trevor Hawkins, MHBC gave a presentation further detailing the proposed development, including the site context and requested zoning by-law amendments. He then responded to questions of Council.

Graham McCormick, Resident of Waterloo spoke on behalf of the neighbourhood about their issues with the development, including the compatibility with the neighbourhood, traffic and pedestrian safety, and proximity to the railway.
Amanda Wyszynski responded to questions of Council.
Christopher Thacker, Resident of Waterloo spoke about minimum parking requirements for the site and the number of parking spaces in the proposal.
As no one else was present to speak to the application, the Chair concluded the Informal Public Meeting and indicated that staff will review the issues and report back to Council at a later date.
Amanda Wyszynski responded to additional questions of Council.

items.title: Notice of Motion
notes: Councillor Wright – Canadian Red Cross Canadian Wildfire Fund Motion Motion tabled September 14, 2026 for Council consideration on September 14, 2026.

items.title: Questions
notes: Councillor Freeman had a question for staff regarding the planned tree planting at Sandowne Park, as people use the slope for tobogganing. Robin Milne responded that there would be a pause on the slope planting to give the team time to reassess.

Councillor Freeman also inquired about a crossing guard on Bridge Street near Chesapeake Drive, where people cross to St. Luke and Lester B Pearson schools. Ron Ormson responded that there are often relief guards available and that they would take a look.

Mayor McCabe had a question about e-scooters, and whether there is legislation or anything that can be done surrounding their speed. Ron Ormson responded that the Province has not put forth legislation yet, but it’s with the City’s Transportation Services.
They are working on different solutions to regulate them within the municipalities.

items.title: New Business
notes: Councillor Freeman informed everyone that the Fox Hunt neighbourhood is holding their party in the park on Sunday, September 20 near Conestoga Mall. They are hoping for good weather.

Councillor Roe mentioned that the Waterloo Infant Toddler Daycare celebrated their 40th anniversary this past weekend. It was a great celebration, with families who once attended the facility now bringing their own children there.

Councillor Wright mentioned a number of events that occurred in the Uptown this past weekend, including the MacGregor Albert Community Association BBQ, the Norman Street Party, the Maker Faire, and the 50th anniversary celebration for Trinidad and Tobago. Across the border in Kitchener, there was also Bestival in Belmont Village and Climate Fest at the Gaukel Block. She added on that Lumen is this coming weekend, September 19, in Waterloo.

motions.text: WHEREAS communities across Canada have been severely impacted by 2026 wildfires causing significant damage, interrupted daily life for those impacted and resulted in loss of life and property; and WHEREAS wildfires are a significant public health issue impacting the physical and mental health of populations with impacts inequitably distributed and disproportionately impacting indigenous communities; and WHEREAS during the summer of 2026, wildfire smoke blanketed the City of Waterloo as southern Ontario experienced air quality conditions that ranked among the worst in the world, demonstrating that communities far from active wildfires are increasingly vulnerable to changing climate driven environmental hazards; and WHEREAS the Canadian Red Cross has an urgent appeal for donations to the Canadian Wildfire Fund; and WHEREAS the fund is intended to enhance Canada’s readiness and response to the escalating wildfire risks and bolster resilience. NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that $15,000 be funded from Council’s Community Priority and Contingency Reserve be donated to the Canadian Red Cross Wildfire fund.
